status: Verified across mod-free vanilla 26.3 and all nine Fabric runtime modes. Adds fixtures function_compiler_probe:mo09_fork_arbitrary_identity and function_compiler_probe:mo09_fork_random_identity plus the identity and freshness block in the harness fork-order fixture runner, and closes the MO-09 row's remaining selector shapes after QUOTA-009 and MO-06 had swept fork caps 0/1/2/4 and the ordered sorts. The oracle was pinned by measuring the pinned vanilla server first: sort=arbitrary resolves candidates in entity insertion (summon) order, not position order - a reverse-summon control (c,b,a) resolved c,b - and that order is stable across repeated invocations, /reload, a server restart on the same world, and fresh worlds with different seeds, which is what makes it oracle-able exactly; sort=random is non-deterministic by design (24 direct trials covered all three candidate pairs 8/8/8 with every trial exactly two distinct actors), so the row's claim for random is narrowed to per-trial set semantics plus a distinct-pair floor across trials proving the fork delegates selection to vanilla's randomness instead of pinning it. The fork cap includes the parent context: for a limit=2 selector cap 1 reports the maximum-context error, cap 2 truncates silently with no feedback, and caps 3+ fork both branches in selection order - the same boundary QUOTA-009 recorded for the ordered sorts. Killing a selected actor must change the next invocation's selection on both paths (candidate-list freshness); killing all actors and re-summoning the canonical sequence restores the pinned order. The fork modifier has no dedicated compile counter, so specialization parity rests on the exact score-state parity of the swap-chain read-backs plus the existing ordered-sort fork fixtures.
